{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "app/serializers/embedding_serializer.rb",
      "line": 3,
      "severity": "critical",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Serializer produces embeddable_hosts as ids but client store expects embeddable_host_ids",
      "body": "The serializer uses `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`, which outputs a key `embeddable_hosts` containing an array of ids. However, the client store's `_hydrateEmbedded` method looks for keys ending in `_ids` (e.g., `embeddable_host_ids`) to hydrate plural associations. As a result, the embedding model will not have its `embeddable_hosts` property set to a collection of models; instead it will contain a plain array of ids. The template `embedding.hbs` iterates over `embedding.embeddable_hosts` and passes each item to the `embeddable-host` component, which expects a model, leading to runtime errors and an empty/broken admin page. The `embed: :ids` option should be removed so that the default rest serializer includes `embeddable_host_ids`, or the client code must be updated to handle the plural association name."
    },
    {
      "file": "db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb",
      "line": 9,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Migration fails if embed_category setting is missing or has no matching category",
      "body": "The migration executes `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` and immediately calls `[0]['id']`. If the `embed_category` site setting does not exist or its value does not match any category name, the query returns no rows, and `[0]` is nil, causing a `NoMethodError` and aborting the migration. This would break upgrades for any forum that has not configured `embed_category` or has it set to a non-existent category. The code should check for the existence of a result before accessing `[0]`."
    },
    {
      "file": "db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb",
      "line": 25,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "SQL injection and missing normalization when migrating host values",
      "body": "The migration uses raw string interpolation to insert host values: `execute \"INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...\"`. This is vulnerable to SQL injection if the old `embeddable_hosts` setting contained a quote. Additionally, the inserted hosts are not normalized (e.g., stripping `http://` or paths), unlike the model's `before_validation` which does so on save. As a result, migrated hosts will not match when `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against the URI host, breaking embed functionality until each record is manually edited and saved. Parameterized queries and application of the same normalization logic should be used."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb",
      "line": 10,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Update action does not handle missing host record",
      "body": "In the `update` action, `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` may return nil if the id is invalid. The code then calls `save_host(host)`, which attempts `host.host = ...` on nil, raising a `NoMethodError` and returning a 500 error. The action should check for nil and return a 404 response with an appropriate error message."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Destroy action does not handle missing host record",
      "body": "Similar to update, `destroy` fetches `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without checking for nil. If the id does not exist, `host.destroy` raises a `NoMethodError`, causing a 500. The controller should return a 404 when the host is not found."
    },
    {
      "file": "spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb",
      "line": 1,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Category and embeddable_host fabricators appear swapped between files",
      "body": "The file `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` instead of category fabricators, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the original category fabricators. This is almost certainly an accidental swap during file creation. While it may still work because Fabrication loads all `.rb` files regardless of name, it is confusing and likely unintended. The category fabricators should be in their own file and the embeddable_host fabricator in its own."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/embeddable_host.rb",
      "line": 6,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "before_validation crashes when host is nil",
      "body": "The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!` and `self.host.sub!` without checking if `host` is nil. If a host record is created or updated with a nil host (e.g., due to missing params), this will raise a `NoMethodError`. The controller always attempts to set `host.host` from `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, but if that param is absent, the value remains nil. The model should handle nil gracefully, either by skipping the callback or adding a presence validation."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb",
      "line": 10,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Update action is a no-op and may mislead the frontend",
      "body": "The `update` action in `Admin::EmbeddingController` simply renders the same `@embedding` serialization without processing any incoming parameters. The frontend calls `embedding.update({})` which triggers a PUT to this endpoint, but no data is persisted. This could cause confusion or mask missing functionality. Either implement actual update logic or remove the route/action to avoid a misleading API."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic.rb",
      "line": 869,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Removal of embeddable_hosts check may expose expandable posts when no hosts configured",
      "body": "The `expandable_first_post?` method previously required `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` in addition to `embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?`. With the removal of that check, if `embed_truncate` is true and a topic has an embed (perhaps from old data), the expandable feature will be enabled even when no embeddable hosts are configured in the new table. This could lead to unexpected UI behavior for forums that have embed_truncate enabled but no allowed hosts."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Serializer produces embeddable_hosts as ids but client store expects embeddable_host_ids
findings.body: The serializer uses `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`, which outputs a key `embeddable_hosts` containing an array of ids. However, the client store's `_hydrateEmbedded` method looks for keys ending in `_ids` (e.g., `embeddable_host_ids`) to hydrate plural associations. As a result, the embedding model will not have its `embeddable_hosts` property set to a collection of models; instead it will contain a plain array of ids. The template `embedding.hbs` iterates over `embedding.embeddable_hosts` and passes each item to the `embeddable-host` component, which expects a model, leading to runtime errors and an empty/broken admin page. The `embed: :ids` option should be removed so that the default rest serializer includes `embeddable_host_ids`, or the client code must be updated to handle the plural association name.

findings.title: Migration fails if embed_category setting is missing or has no matching category
findings.body: The migration executes `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` and immediately calls `[0]['id']`. If the `embed_category` site setting does not exist or its value does not match any category name, the query returns no rows, and `[0]` is nil, causing a `NoMethodError` and aborting the migration. This would break upgrades for any forum that has not configured `embed_category` or has it set to a non-existent category. The code should check for the existence of a result before accessing `[0]`.

findings.title: SQL injection and missing normalization when migrating host values
findings.body: The migration uses raw string interpolation to insert host values: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ..."`. This is vulnerable to SQL injection if the old `embeddable_hosts` setting contained a quote. Additionally, the inserted hosts are not normalized (e.g., stripping `http://` or paths), unlike the model's `before_validation` which does so on save. As a result, migrated hosts will not match when `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` against the URI host, breaking embed functionality until each record is manually edited and saved. Parameterized queries and application of the same normalization logic should be used.

findings.title: Update action does not handle missing host record
findings.body: In the `update` action, `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` may return nil if the id is invalid. The code then calls `save_host(host)`, which attempts `host.host = ...` on nil, raising a `NoMethodError` and returning a 500 error. The action should check for nil and return a 404 response with an appropriate error message.

findings.title: Destroy action does not handle missing host record
findings.body: Similar to update, `destroy` fetches `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without checking for nil. If the id does not exist, `host.destroy` raises a `NoMethodError`, causing a 500. The controller should return a 404 when the host is not found.

findings.title: Category and embeddable_host fabricators appear swapped between files
findings.body: The file `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now contains `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` instead of category fabricators, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the original category fabricators. This is almost certainly an accidental swap during file creation. While it may still work because Fabrication loads all `.rb` files regardless of name, it is confusing and likely unintended. The category fabricators should be in their own file and the embeddable_host fabricator in its own.

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` block calls `self.host.sub!` and `self.host.sub!` without checking if `host` is nil. If a host record is created or updated with a nil host (e.g., due to missing params), this will raise a `NoMethodError`. The controller always attempts to set `host.host` from `params[:embeddable_host][:host]`, but if that param is absent, the value remains nil. The model should handle nil gracefully, either by skipping the callback or adding a presence validation.

findings.title: Update action is a no-op and may mislead the frontend
findings.body: The `update` action in `Admin::EmbeddingController` simply renders the same `@embedding` serialization without processing any incoming parameters. The frontend calls `embedding.update({})` which triggers a PUT to this endpoint, but no data is persisted. This could cause confusion or mask missing functionality. Either implement actual update logic or remove the route/action to avoid a misleading API.

findings.title: Removal of embeddable_hosts check may expose expandable posts when no hosts configured
findings.body: The `expandable_first_post?` method previously required `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` in addition to `embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?`. With the removal of that check, if `embed_truncate` is true and a topic has an embed (perhaps from old data), the expandable feature will be enabled even when no embeddable hosts are configured in the new table. This could lead to unexpected UI behavior for forums that have embed_truncate enabled but no allowed hosts.
